newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends off as Cenbnk lets it slip.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends off as Cenbnk lets it slip.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar slipped for the third day running to close at 479/478 per dollar as the Central Bank stood back once more from the session limiting itself to only small dollar sales, traders said.
After the bolivar virtually traded flat last week: "I think this is a signal ... the Central Bank want the month to close with the boliver at 482 per dollar," said one trader.
"Each time today that the Bank sold dollars it did so at a higher rate. By contrast last week it would just come in with a splash at the end of the day to firm the exchange rate," he added.
Traders said boliver weakness was added to by a 206 basis points back-up in benchmark six month TEMs yields to 16.1 percent in Wednesday's regular Central Bank auction.
But New York-based IDEA analysts service said low trade volume suggested the bolivar's drop was not indicative of outflows due to the fall in TEM rates.

While foreign investors "remain concerned that the Central Bank is correcting for the bolivar's strong overvaluation ... we maintain that the strong bolivar is the Bank's most effective and affordable tool to fight inflation," it said in market comment.
"As such, we do not expect to see bolivar weakness to intensify."
